source: A real attached session (`01a1f0af-1716-…`, room WF-jI-uORO6x) recorded by the web client itself: loaded with `?capture=1`, which tees every inbound envelope to `window.__unbienFrames` (web-client/src/app.ts). `raw.jsonl` is that dump — UNSCRUBBED, and deliberately not committed: it holds raw prompts, reasoning text and a pairing payload. `capture.py` turns it into the two committed inputs.
scrub: Field-aware, spelled out in capture.py. Content fields (`text`, `thinking`, `summary`, `delta`, `errorMessage`, base64 image `data`) and every value under `details` (a pairing token in a fixture is a credential in a repository) become LENGTH-PRESERVING filler of the U+2591 block-shade character; `sessionId` too, since it names a real room on a real relay and no fold needs it. Any other string over the 48-char readable cap is filled as well. Filler rather than a `«length»` marker is deliberate HERE and only here: the two planes' text must be comparable as strings (the durable plane gives one content block, the live plane gives the deltas that built it), and a marker per delta would make the joined text incomparable. Entry ids, parentIds, toolCallIds, correlation ids, roles, tool names, mimeTypes, timestamps, stopReasons and usage numbers are verbatim.
description: The paired fixture: ONE session, ONE instant, TWO arrivals. `input.jsonl` is everything the connected client received, in order — the attach walk, one live turn (a 6-step tool probe: read, bash, write, edit, read, bash, so the tool faces, an `aux.hunks` sidecar and streaming deltas are all in it), the five post-turn resync walks, and a final walk. `replay.jsonl` is ONLY that final walk: 87 durable entries plus the empty terminal page carrying the active-leaf beacon (`69be0624`) — the whole view of a client that arrives cold at the end of the window and never sees a live frame. Both runs must land on the same transcript: same rows, same row keys, same leaf. This is what 'identical across modes' has always promised and no scenario had ever tested, and it exercises the machinery the single-plane fixtures cannot: live rows keyed `assistant#3` then RE-KEYED to pi's durable entry id by a walk, late births inserting before anchored rows, and a walk re-folded while its own rows are already on screen.
note: No frame in either file is authored; every line is something the wire actually sent. Three findings this fixture produced, kept here so nobody re-derives them: (1) THINKING GAP. pi persists `thinking` blocks ON the message entry — 25 of them in this session — and neither fold turns a persisted block into a row: reasoning rows exist only where the deltas were watched, so a client that attaches cold shows a transcript with every thinking row missing. The projection cannot express the equality either (`ConformanceProjection.swift:95` keys reasoning rows synthetic `reasoning#n` unconditionally, `replayStable: false`). Filed as a design question, not papered over. (2) THE DELTA GUARD. Both folds drop a `message_update` frame identical to the last one applied, as a redelivery guard (reference `SessionState.swift:457`, added after run 2026-09-18 'every chunk repeats'). With this model `usage` is all-zero and adjacent frames can share a `ts`, so scrubbed fixtures can contain byte-identical frames and the guard eats a legitimate chunk of text — under the projection's 48-char text window the loss is invisible. It is a real hazard on the wire too, not only in fixtures. This client's guard used to compare only `type|delta`, which is stricter than the reference and dropped two deltas where the reference dropped one; it now uses the same full-frame rule. (3) SIDECAR LOSS. `aux.hunks` rides `tool_execution_start`, but a streamed tool call usually opens its card earlier from a `toolcall_start` delta, which carries no aux. Attaching the sidecar only when creating the card lost it for good: the reference projected `[diff, hunks]` and this client `[diff]`. Fixed in `startTool`, pinned by a reducer test. (4) The walk pages repeat — the client re-walks the whole history after every turn, so the same 87 entries arrive six times. That redundancy is kept on purpose: a fold that appends per page instead of replacing the set fails here.
pairing: The pair is asserted three ways in both runners: cold run vs golden, cold run vs the reference's own cold fold, and the two runs against each other. Three parts of the projection are dropped from the cross-plane comparison, each for a stated reason rather than by silence: `panels`/`subagents`/`pendingAsks` (pi does not persist them, so a cold arrival has none by construction); `reasoning` rows (see note); the `hunks` block on a tool card (the diff sidecar rides the live `tool_execution_start` frame and nothing else, so a cold card settles to `[diff]` where a watched one settles to `[diff, hunks]`).
